clips.send: Air molecules (the medium). Pass the vibration along. Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium — a solid, liquid or gas — to travel through. Each molecule just jiggles back and forth around its place and bumps the next one. The molecules do not fly from the speaker to your ear. Sound travels faster in liquids and fastest in solids, because their particles are closer together: air about 343 m/s, water about 1480 m/s, steel about 5960 m/s.
clips.text: Air molecules (the medium). Pass the vibration along. Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium — a solid, liquid or gas — to travel through.. Each molecule just jiggles back and forth around its place and bumps the next one. The molecules do not fly from the speaker to your ear.. Sound travels faster in liquids and fastest in solids, because their particles are closer together: air ≈ 343 m/s, water ≈ 1480 m/s, steel ≈ 5960 m/s.

clips.send: Eardrum. Vibrates with the sound wave. The eardrum is a thin, tight membrane, like the skin of a drum. Compressions push it in, rarefactions let it move out, so it vibrates at the same frequency as the sound. Louder sounds make it vibrate with a bigger amplitude.
clips.text: Eardrum. Vibrates with the sound wave. The eardrum is a thin, tight membrane, like the skin of a drum.. Compressions push it in, rarefactions let it move out, so it vibrates at the same frequency as the sound.. Louder sounds make it vibrate with a bigger amplitude.

clips.send: Auditory nerve, brain. Carries signals to the brain. The auditory nerve carries electrical signals from the cochlea to the brain. The brain interprets the signals as pitch, loudness and the kind of sound — a voice, music or a dog barking. Using two ears lets the brain work out where a sound is coming from.
clips.text: Auditory nerve → brain. Carries signals to the brain. The auditory nerve carries electrical signals from the cochlea to the brain.. The brain interprets the signals as pitch, loudness and the kind of sound — a voice, music or a dog barking.. Using two ears lets the brain work out where a sound is coming from.

clips.send: Outer ear (pinna). Collects sound waves. The curved outer ear acts like a funnel, gathering sound waves and directing them into the ear canal. Its shape also helps your brain tell whether a sound comes from in front or behind. Animals like rabbits and cats can turn their outer ears toward a sound.
clips.text: Outer ear (pinna). Collects sound waves. The curved outer ear acts like a funnel, gathering sound waves and directing them into the ear canal.. Its shape also helps your brain tell whether a sound comes from in front or behind.. Animals like rabbits and cats can turn their outer ears toward a sound.

clips.send: Compression. Air squeezed together. A compression is a region where air molecules are crowded together, at slightly higher pressure. Sound is a longitudinal wave: the molecules vibrate in the same direction the wave travels. The distance from one compression to the next is one wavelength. For a fixed speed, higher pitch, shorter wavelength.

Sound is a longitudinal wave: the molecules vibrate in the same direction the wave travels.. The distance from one compression to the next is one wavelength. clips.send: Ear canal. Carries sound to the eardrum. The ear canal is a tube about 2.5 cm long that leads from the outer ear to the eardrum. It contains earwax, which traps dust and protects the ear. Never push objects into your ear canal: you could damage the eardrum.

clips.send: Ossicles (hammer, anvil, stirrup). Amplify the vibrations. Three tiny bones in the middle ear: the hammer (malleus), anvil (incus) and stirrup (stapes). They act like levers, passing the vibrations from the eardrum to the cochlea and making them stronger. The stirrup is the smallest bone in the human body — about 3 mm long.

clips.send: Speaker cone (vibration). Every sound starts with a vibration. The speaker cone moves back and forth very fast. Each push squeezes the air in front of it; each pull spreads it out. How many times per second it vibrates is the frequency, measured in hertz (Hz). How far it moves (the amplitude) decides how loud the sound is.

How many times per second it vibrates is the frequency, measured in hertz (Hz).. How far it moves (the amplitude) decides how loud the sound is.

clips.send: Rarefaction. Air spread apart. A rarefaction is a region where air molecules are spread out, at slightly lower pressure. Compressions and rarefactions alternate as the wave moves outward from the source. Your eardrum is pushed in by compressions and pulled out by rarefactions.
clips.text: Rarefaction. Air spread apart. A rarefaction is a region where air molecules are spread out, at slightly lower pressure.. Compressions and rarefactions alternate as the wave moves outward from the source.. Your eardrum is pushed in by compressions and pulled out by rarefactions.

clips.send: Cochlea. Turns vibrations into nerve signals. The cochlea is a snail-shaped tube filled with fluid and lined with thousands of tiny hair cells. Vibrations make waves in the fluid; the hair cells bend and send electrical signals. High pitches are detected near the start of the spiral, low pitches near the tip — watch the glowing spot move as you change the pitch.

clips.send: 密部。被挤紧的空气。密部是空气分子挤在一起、压强稍高的区域。声波是纵波：分子的振动方向与波的传播方向相同。相邻两个密部之间的距离就是一个波长。波速一定时，音调越高，波长越短。
clips.text: 密部. 被挤紧的空气. 密部是空气分子挤在一起、压强稍高的区域。. 声波是纵波：分子的振动方向与波的传播方向相同。. 相邻两个密部之间的距离就是一个波长。波速一定时，音调越高，波长越短。

clips.send: 空气分子（介质）。把振动传递下去。声音是机械波，需要介质（固体、液体或气体）才能传播。每个分子只是在原位置附近前后振动，并撞击下一个分子。分子并不会从扬声器一路飞到你的耳朵里。声音在液体中传得更快，在固体中最快，因为它们的粒子靠得更近：空气约 343 m/s，水约 1480 m/s，钢约 5960 m/s。
clips.text: 空气分子（介质）. 把振动传递下去. 声音是机械波，需要介质（固体、液体或气体）才能传播。. 每个分子只是在原位置附近前后振动，并撞击下一个分子。分子并不会从扬声器一路飞到你的耳朵里。. 声音在液体中传得更快，在固体中最快，因为它们的粒子靠得更近：空气约 343 m/s，水约 1480 m/s，钢约 5960 m/s。

clips.send: 扬声器纸盆（振动）。所有的声音都始于振动。扬声器纸盆飞快地前后振动。每向前推一次，就把前方的空气挤紧；每向后拉一次，就让空气变稀疏。每秒振动的次数叫频率，单位是赫兹，Hz。振动的幅度（振幅）决定声音有多响。
clips.text: 扬声器纸盆（振动）. 所有的声音都始于振动. 扬声器纸盆飞快地前后振动。每向前推一次，就把前方的空气挤紧；每向后拉一次，就让空气变稀疏。. 每秒振动的次数叫频率，单位是赫兹（Hz）。. 振动的幅度（振幅）决定声音有多响。

clips.send: 外耳（耳廓）。收集声波。弯曲的耳廓像漏斗一样，把声波收集起来，引入耳道。耳廓的形状还能帮助大脑判断声音来自前方还是后方。兔子和猫等动物能把耳廓转向声音的方向。
clips.text: 外耳（耳廓）. 收集声波. 弯曲的耳廓像漏斗一样，把声波收集起来，引入耳道。. 耳廓的形状还能帮助大脑判断声音来自前方还是后方。. 兔子和猫等动物能把耳廓转向声音的方向。

clips.send: 鼓膜。随声波一起振动。鼓膜是一层又薄又紧的膜，就像鼓面一样。密部把它向里推，疏部让它向外移，所以它以和声音相同的频率振动。声音越响，鼓膜振动的幅度越大。
clips.text: 鼓膜. 随声波一起振动. 鼓膜是一层又薄又紧的膜，就像鼓面一样。. 密部把它向里推，疏部让它向外移，所以它以和声音相同的频率振动。. 声音越响，鼓膜振动的幅度越大。

clips.send: 耳道。把声音传到鼓膜。耳道是一条约 2.5 厘米长的管道，从外耳通向鼓膜。耳道里有耳垢，可以粘住灰尘、保护耳朵。千万不要把东西塞进耳道，可能会损伤鼓膜。
clips.text: 耳道. 把声音传到鼓膜. 耳道是一条约 2.5 厘米长的管道，从外耳通向鼓膜。. 耳道里有耳垢，可以粘住灰尘、保护耳朵。. 千万不要把东西塞进耳道，可能会损伤鼓膜。

clips.send: 疏部。变稀疏的空气。疏部是空气分子分散开、压强稍低的区域。声波从声源向外传播时，密部和疏部交替出现。密部把鼓膜向里推，疏部把鼓膜向外拉。
clips.text: 疏部. 变稀疏的空气. 疏部是空气分子分散开、压强稍低的区域。. 声波从声源向外传播时，密部和疏部交替出现。. 密部把鼓膜向里推，疏部把鼓膜向外拉。

clips.send: 耳蜗。把振动转化为神经信号。耳蜗是一条像蜗牛壳一样的管道，里面充满液体，排列着成千上万个微小的毛细胞。振动在液体中形成波，毛细胞弯曲后发出电信号。高音由螺旋起始处感受，低音由螺旋顶端感受——改变音调，看看发光点怎样移动。
clips.text: 耳蜗. 把振动转化为神经信号. 耳蜗是一条像蜗牛壳一样的管道，里面充满液体，排列着成千上万个微小的毛细胞。. 振动在液体中形成波，毛细胞弯曲后发出电信号。. 高音由螺旋起始处感受，低音由螺旋顶端感受——改变音调，看看发光点怎样移动。

clips.send: 听小骨（锤骨、砧骨、镫骨）。放大振动。中耳里有三块小骨头：锤骨、砧骨和镫骨。它们像杠杆一样，把鼓膜的振动传给耳蜗，并把振动放大。镫骨是人体最小的骨头，只有约 3 毫米长。

clips.send: 听神经，大脑。把信号传给大脑。听神经把电信号从耳蜗传到大脑。大脑把这些信号解读为音调、响度和声音的种类，比如说话声、音乐或狗叫声。两只耳朵一起工作，大脑就能判断声音从哪里来。
